claims.claim: Aza Raskin designed infinite scroll in 2006.
claims.episode_span: In 2006 Aza Raskin designed and championed the infinite-scroll pattern
claims.source_title: Social media apps are 'deliberately' addictive to users - BBC News
claims.supporting_quote: In 2006 Mr Raskin, a leading technology engineer himself, designed infinite scroll, one of the features of many apps that is now seen as highly habit forming.

claims.claim: Infinite scroll lets users move endlessly through content without clicking to load another page.
claims.episode_span: Instead of clicking a “next” button to load another page, the content would simply continue as the user scrolled downward
claims.source_title: Social media apps are 'deliberately' addictive to users - BBC News
claims.supporting_quote: Infinite scroll allows users to endlessly swipe down through content without clicking.

claims.claim: Raskin later publicly criticized habit-forming interface design, comparing engagement features to 'behavioural cocaine' (BBC, 2018).
claims.episode_span: By the late 2010s Raskin began speaking publicly about the regret, describing infinite scroll as an invention he wished he could retract
claims.source_title: Social media apps are 'deliberately' addictive to users - BBC News
claims.supporting_quote: It's as if they're taking behavioural cocaine and just sprinkling it all over your interface and that's the thing that keeps you like coming back and back and back

claims.claim: YouTube began testing autoplay of suggested videos on select users' accounts in December 2014, ahead of its wider rollout.
claims.episode_span: YouTube rolled auto-play out globally in 2015 after smaller experiments on its recommendation bar
claims.source_title: YouTube Tests Autoplay Feature For Next-Up Suggested Videos - Tubefilter
claims.supporting_quote: This time, the video site is implementing a test-run of autoplay video suggestions on select users’ accounts.

claims.claim: YouTube's autoplay toggle was set to 'on' by default, though users could switch it off.
claims.episode_span: YouTube shipped auto-play with an off switch from the start, but the toggle defaulted to on
claims.source_title: YouTube Tests Autoplay Feature For Next-Up Suggested Videos - Tubefilter
claims.supporting_quote: The autoplay toggle is set to “on” by default, but users have the ability to switch it off before the next video plays.
